UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                     BEFORE THE
                       FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

     PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                             )                 Docket No. ER26-3380-000

             MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND LIMITED ANSWER OF
                       FIRSTENERGY SERVICE COMPANY

         Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”),1 FirstEnergy Service Company

(“FirstEnergy”) respectfully files this Limited Answer in response to the answer to comments and

protests submitted by PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) on September 10, 2026 (the

“September 10 PJM Answer”), in this proceeding on PJM’s proposal to establish a Reliability

Backstop Procurement (“RBP”) mechanism.2

I.       Answer

         Although the September 10 PJM Answer purports to respond to the points made in the

August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest,3 PJM fails to advance facts or law that satisfy its

burden of proof under section 205 of the Federal Power Act (the “FPA”) to demonstrate that the

July 31 RBP Proposal is just and reasonable.4 As explained in the August 21 FirstEnergy



1
         18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, 385.213.
2
          PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address Resource Adequacy Concerns Stemming from Large
Loads, Docket No. ER26-3380-000 (the “July 31 RBP Proposal”). On August 20, 2026 FirstEnergy filed, as agent
for its franchised public utility and transmission-owning public utility affiliates, a motion to intervene in this
proceeding. On August 21, 2026, FirstEnergy filed comments and a protest regarding the July 31 RBP Proposal (the
“August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest”).
         FirstEnergy respectfully requests waiver of Rule 213(a)(2), 18 C.F.R. § 385.213(a)(2), to permit it to file this
Limited Answer to the September 10 PJM Answer. Good cause for the waiver exists because this limited answer will
aid the Commission in understanding the issues in the proceeding, inform the Commission in its decision-making
process, and help to ensure a complete and accurate record in the case. See, e.g., PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 187
FERC ¶ 61,173, at P 25 (2024); Constellation Mystic Power, LLC, 185 FERC ¶ 61,016, at P 14 (2023); ISO New Eng.
Inc., 175 FERC ¶ 61,172, at P 15 (2021).
3
         See September 10 PJM Answer at 59, 63-67, 74-76, 79-82, 88, 89 n.271.
4
         See August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest at 1-2.
 Comments and Protest, there are a number of ways in which PJM has not met its burden of proof.5

The September 10 PJM Answer does not repair those defects. Among other deficiencies, PJM’s

answer fails to explain or address how its proposal could possibly be just and reasonable if it does

not actually allocate RBP-related costs to the new data centers driving the need for such capacity,

in accordance with the NEDC/PJM Governors’ Statement of Principles that underlies the RBP

proposal.6

         Accordingly, FirstEnergy reiterates that the Commission grant the relief requested in the

August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest: the Commission should reject the July 31 RBP

Proposal, institute a proceeding under section 206 of the FPA, and establish settlement

proceedings.7 Alternatively, even if the Commission were to accept the July 31 RBP Proposal for

filing, such acceptance should be conditioned on PJM submitting a subsequent compliance filing

that addresses the issues raised in the August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest.




5

         August 21 FirstEnergy Comments and Protest at 22.

 II.    Conclusion

       For the foregoing reasons and the reasons explained in the August 21 FirstEnergy

Comments and Protest, FirstEnergy respectfully requests that the Commission grant the relief

requested herein.
